headline: Thursday Night Football: Texans stifle Colts 26-3 to seize command of AFC South
teaser: C.J. Stroud throws two touchdown passes and Houston's relentless pass rush forces three turnovers, limiting Anthony Richardson to 112 passing yards in a 26-3 blowout.
story:
The Houston Texans delivered a resounding defensive masterclass on Thursday night, 19 November, smothering the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 at NRG Stadium to solidify their position atop the AFC South.

Quarterback C.J. Stroud was clinical under the prime-time lights, completing 22 of 29 passes for 248 yards and two touchdowns without a turnover. Meanwhile, Houston's defense suffocated the Colts, holding Anthony Richardson to just 112 yards through the air and intercepting him twice. Running back Jonathan Taylor was held to 48 yards on 14 carries as Indianapolis failed to reach the end zone all night.

With the 26-3 rout, Houston improves to 7-4 and sweeps the season tiebreaker against Indianapolis (6-5), giving the Texans a commanding edge in the divisional championship race as Week 11 action heads toward Sunday.
whyCareReason: Houston dominates their fiercest division rival 26-3 to seize total control of the AFC South tiebreaker.
stakes: The Texans (7-4) take a full game lead in the AFC South, while the Colts (6-5) slide into the wild card bubble.
rivalryAngle: Houston held Indianapolis without a touchdown for the first time in their last nine head-to-head meetings.
funFacts: Houston's defense recorded four sacks and three total turnovers on Thursday night.
C.J. Stroud has now thrown multiple touchdown passes in five consecutive games against AFC South opponents.
The 23-point margin of victory is Houston's largest over Indianapolis since 2012.
